title: Microsoft Purview DLP: SLA-based alert reporting dashboard
summary: The briefing accurately separates Microsoft's planned SLA dashboard from the existing DLP alert tools, and its rollout targets match the roadmap. The commands, alert licensing and retention statements are supported; two admin paths stop early at the correct location and should be extended to the settings.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview SLA dashboard license pricing subscription'; read Purview service description, DLP alerts licensing, alerts dashboard and DLP overview. Workload and alert-configuration entitlements are documented, but no entitlement for the planned SLA dashboard was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price for this SLA dashboard.

claims.claim: The existing DLP Alerts dashboard is reached in the Microsoft Purview portal through Data loss prevention > Alerts.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention.
2. Select Alerts to view the DLP Alerts dashboard.

claims.claim: The existing DLP Alerts dashboard lets analysts view alerts.
claims.quote: You use the DLP alert management dashboard in the Microsoft Purview portal to view alerts, events, and associated metadata for DLP policy violations.

claims.claim: The existing DLP Alerts dashboard supports filtering alerts.
claims.quote: Use the Filter fields to refine the list of alerts.

claims.claim: The existing DLP Alerts dashboard supports assigning alert ownership.
claims.quote: After you investigate the alert, return to the Overview tab where you can View details to triage and manage the disposition of the alert, add comments and assign ownership of the alert.

claims.claim: Analysts can set an alert's Status to Resolved in the existing dashboard.
claims.quote: After you take the required action for the alert, set the Status of the alert to Resolved.

claims.claim: Alert policy details already list sensitive information types detected in a policy match.
claims.quote: | sensitive information types (SIT) detected | SITs that were detected as part of the DLP policy match | all events |

claims.claim: DLP posture reports in the Microsoft Purview portal are in preview.
claims.quote: Information Protection posture reports, Data Loss Prevention posture reports, and Custom posture reports are in preview. The capabilities, terminology, and UX may change before general availability.

claims.claim: DLP posture reports include most triggered DLP rules and activities.
claims.quote:
Data Loss Prevention posture reports

These reports are in preview.

- Most triggered DLP rules and activities

claims.claim: Posture reports use a 30-day rolling window.
claims.quote: The data shown in posture reports is gathered on a 30-day rolling-window basis. Save any reports (as .PDF) that you want to keep for future reference.

claims.claim: The cited descriptions of existing DLP alerts and posture reports do not mention SLA targets or time-to-respond metrics.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview SLA alert dashboard' and 'Purview MTTA MTTD MTTR'; read the DLP alerts dashboard, DLP alerts and posture reports pages. They document alert handling and activity reports, not SLA targets or time-to-respond metrics.

claims.claim: DLP alerts are available in the Microsoft Purview DLP alerts dashboard for 30 days.
claims.quote: DLP alerts are available in the Microsoft Defender portal for six months. They're only available in the Microsoft Purview DLP alerts dashboard for 30 days.

claims.claim: A DLP rule's ReportSeverityLevel accepts None, Low, Medium or High.
claims.quote:
The ReportSeverityLevel parameter specifies the severity level of the incident report for content detections based on the rule. Valid values are:
- None: You can't select this value if the rule has no actions configured.
- Low: This value is the default.
- Medium
- High

claims.claim: None cannot be selected as ReportSeverityLevel if the rule has no actions configured.
claims.quote: None: You can't select this value if the rule has no actions configured.

claims.claim: The severity setting under Incident reports is labelled Use this severity level in admin alerts and reports.
claims.quote:
Under Incident reports:
1. Set Use this severity level in admin alerts and reports to Low.

claims.claim: The rule severity control is reached through Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies > policy > Edit policy > Customize advanced DLP rules > rule > Incident reports.
claims.quote:
Go to the Customize advanced DLP rules page and edit the Low volume of content detected scenarios U.S. PII Data Enhanced.
5. Scroll down to the Incident reports section
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and the rendered row to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > policy > Edit policy > Customize advanced DLP rules > rule > Incident reports > Use this severity level in admin alerts and reports'. Set ui.docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-external, which documents the final setting; retain the already cited endpoint procedure for the route into the existing rule.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule> -ReportSeverityLevel High modifies the identified DLP rule's report severity.
claims.quote:
The ReportSeverityLevel parameter specifies the severity level of the incident report for content detections based on the rule. Valid values are:
- None: You can't select this value if the rule has no actions configured.
- Low: This value is the default.
- Medium
- High

claims.claim: DLP alert role-group membership is managed in Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups.
claims.quote:
Go to Settings > Roles and scopes to view and manage compliance and governance roles in your organization.
2. Select Role groups.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the rendered row to 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions. The current path stops on the correct list but does not reach membership editing.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds the specified user to the specified role group.
claims.quote:
Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group.
The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to.
The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group.

claims.claim: The documented portal procedure for changing role-group membership requires the Role management role.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role.

claims.claim: Learn lists Compliance Administrator, Security Administrator, Security Reader and Information Protection Analyst among the role groups for viewing the existing DLP dashboard or editing alert configuration.
claims.quote:
- Compliance Administrator

- Security Operator

claims.claim: Learn also documents dashboard access through Manage alerts plus either DLP Compliance Management or View-Only DLP Compliance Management.
